text:
Beckett Sennecke came back from a short day-to-day stint for tonight's Kings game, and Hockey.com reported he practised on Anaheim's top power play beforehand. That is where he has made his leap.

At 20, in his second season, the third overall pick from 2024 has 12 goals and 26 points in 22 games, up from 0.73 points a game last season to 1.18. He plays over 20 minutes a night now, almost three more than a year ago, and he is on the ice for 82% of the Ducks' power-play chances, up from 47%. Of the forwards taken in the top five since 2005, the median first full season was 0.54 points a game.

Some of it will cool. His shooting is at 22.6%, against a likely range around 14%, and the Ducks have scored 11 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there, one of the bigger luck cushions in the league. But the chances are real: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile for chances from the home-plate area last season, and his on-ice expected goals over his last ten are well above his norm. The points will come down; the player is not a mirage.
